title: Multi-Tier Racking

sections.heading: What Is Multi-Tier Racking?
sections.body: Multi-Tier Racking is a high-rise pedestrian storage and order-picking system that uses full-height vertical racking or heavy shelving uprights to support one, two, or three suspended upper floor walkways directly within the racking footprint. Many warehouses have generous 6-metre to 12-metre roof heights, yet standard hand-picked shelving stops at around 2.1 metres because operatives on the ground cannot reach higher without slow mobile steps. Multi-Tier Racking solves this wasted overhead space by stacking complete pedestrian picking levels on top of one another—connected by staircases and pallet loading gates—effectively doubling or tripling your hand-picking floor capacity without pouring concrete or extending your building.

sections.heading: How Multi-Tier Racking Works
sections.body: Unlike a traditional structural steel mezzanine floor where shelving is placed loosely on top of a wide-span steel platform, Multi-Tier Racking uses the vertical storage uprights themselves as the primary load-bearing columns from ground level right up to the top tier. Horizontal steel floor joists bracket directly onto the racking uprights between aisles at 2.2m to 2.5m vertical intervals, supporting heavy-duty 38mm high-density floor boarding or open galvanised steel grating panels that let light and sprinkler water pass through. Staircases, perimeter tubular handrails, kickplates, and up-and-over pallet safety gates allow forklifts to replenish upper tiers while pickers walk every level.

sections.heading: Where Multi-Tier Racking Is Used
sections.body: Multi-Tier Racking transforms high-volume manual picking across the UK. E-commerce clothing, footwear, and fashion fulfilment centres use two-tier and three-tier pick towers to house hundreds of thousands of boxed and hanging garment SKUs within a compact warehouse footprint. Automotive aftermarket and engineering spare parts hubs use multi-tier systems to store small components on upper walkways while keeping heavy engine blocks on the ground floor. Archival record management companies use floor-to-ceiling multi-tier aisles to store tens of thousands of document boxes per warehouse. Electrical, plumbing, and pharmaceutical distributors also use it to double their small-parts picking faces.

sections.heading: Key Considerations
sections.body: Because all the dead weight of the upper walkway floors, live pedestrian loads, and multiple levels of stocked shelves channel straight down through the racking upright baseplates into the ground, a thorough concrete slab point-load calculation is mandatory. Building Control approval, fire detection, smoke ventilation, emergency lighting, and maximum travel distances to fire-protected staircases must all be engineered alongside SEMA structural design codes, which we evaluate during our site survey.

faqs.a: Multi-Tier Racking typically costs between £120 and £240 per square metre of created upper floor footprint (or roughly £250 to £500 per multi-tier bay module), including the full-height racking uprights, shelf levels, suspended walkway flooring, staircases, handrails, and safety pallet gates.

faqs.a: A freestanding mezzanine floor uses wide-span structural steel RSJ columns so you have open floor space underneath for offices or packing benches. title: Timber Decking

sections.heading: What Is Timber Decking?
sections.body: Timber Decking for pallet racking consists of heavy-duty wooden slatted panels or high-density structural chipboard boards designed to sit across the horizontal front and rear steel beams of a pallet racking bay. On standard bare pallet racking, a pallet is supported solely by its extreme front and back edges resting on two narrow steel beams with open air in the middle. Whenever a warehouse handles undersized Euro pallets, four-way post pallets, metal stillages, damaged pallet skids, or hand-picked cartons, loads can easily slip between the bare beams and fall. Timber Decking solves this by turning open beam pairs into solid or slatted load-bearing platforms.

sections.heading: How Timber Decking Works
sections.body: Racking Timber Decking is manufactured in two primary configurations: open-boarded slatted softwood decks and close-boarded solid decks. Open-boarded decks are built from kiln-dried, structural-grade planed timber slats (typically 25mm to 38mm thick) secured onto underside wooden batten retainers. When dropped onto a pair of standard box beams, those underside battens sit snugly against the inner edges of the front and rear steel beams, locking the deck panel laterally so it cannot slide forward or backward when a forklift pushes a pallet into position. For step beams or flush hand-picking levels, 25mm to 38mm structural chipboard panels drop directly into the beam step.

sections.heading: Where Timber Decking Is Used
sections.body: Timber Decking is fitted across thousands of UK warehouses to improve safety and versatility. Third-party logistics (3PL) operators install open-boarded timber decks on all beam levels so forklift drivers can safely place mixed 1200x800mm Euro pallets, 1200x1000mm UK pallets, and custom export skids onto the same 900mm or 1100mm deep rack frames without adjusting beams. Engineering and automotive factories use thick close-boarded decks to support point-loaded steel stillages and wire mesh cages. Furniture, carpet, and white-goods distributors use flush timber decks to protect bulky cartons from beam-edge indentations, while builders' merchants and wholesalers use them to convert lower pallet levels into manual picking shelves.

sections.heading: Key Considerations
sections.body: When ordering Timber Decking, it is critical to distinguish between Uniformly Distributed Loads (UDLs) spread across the whole deck versus concentrated point loads exerted by four-footed steel stillages, which require thicker 32mm or 38mm structural timber slats. You must measure exact outer beam-to-beam frame depth and internal beam thickness so the underside retaining battens fit tightly, and verify whether fire sprinkler policies allow timber or require a 50% open slat gap during our site survey.

faqs.a: Timber Decking is typically 25% to 35% more economical than steel mesh decking and provides a smoother, solid wooden surface for sliding cardboard cartons by hand. Galvanised Steel Mesh Decking costs slightly more, but offers non-combustible fire compliance, 70% open air for ceiling sprinklers, and higher hygiene for food stores.

title: Galvanised Steel Mesh Decking

sections.heading: What Is Galvanised Steel Mesh Decking?
sections.body: Galvanised Steel Mesh Decking—commonly called wire mesh racking decks—is a heavy-duty, non-combustible steel grid panel engineered to drop directly onto pallet racking beams to create a secure shelf surface across open bays. While bare pallet racking beams only support full-sized pallets placed squarely across the front and back beams, wire mesh decking bridges the open space in the middle of the rack. It solves the dual problem of preventing undersized pallets, weak skids, or loose cartons from falling through the racking while simultaneously allowing overhead fire sprinkler water, warehouse lighting, and cold-store airflow to penetrate freely from ceiling to floor.

sections.heading: How Galvanised Steel Mesh Decking Works
sections.body: Each Galvanised Steel Mesh Decking panel is fabricated from heavy-gauge drawn steel wire welded into a rigid rectangular grid (typically 50x100mm or 50x50mm mesh apertures) and reinforced underneath by three or four roll-formed steel V-channel support ribs welded across the underside. The front and rear edges of the mesh feature a turned-down 'waterfall' lip that hooks neatly over the top outer face of the pallet racking box beams, while flared ends on the underside V-channels rest directly on top of the beam ledges. This self-locating waterfall design locks the panel firmly in place without tools or fixings while preventing beams from spreading apart under load.

sections.heading: Where Galvanised Steel Mesh Decking Is Used
sections.body: Galvanised Steel Mesh Decking is specified across safety-critical and hygiene-focused UK warehouses. High-bay distribution centres protected by ESFR ceiling sprinkler systems use mesh decks to satisfy commercial fire insurers who mandate at least 50% to 70% open vertical water flow through every rack level. Food, beverage, and pharmaceutical warehouses use corrosion-resistant zinc-galvanised mesh decks because they do not harbour dust, wood splinters, mould, or pests. Cold storage and blast freezer operators rely on mesh grids to let chilled air circulate evenly around palletised produce. Chemical, paint, and aerosol stores use non-combustible steel mesh to eliminate flammable timber fuel loads, while automotive stores use heavy-duty mesh for metal stillages.

sections.heading: Key Considerations
sections.body: When selecting Galvanised Steel Mesh Decking, you must verify whether your loads are standard Uniformly Distributed Loads (UDLs) from flat-bottomed pallets or concentrated point loads from small-wheeled cages or four-legged post stillages, which require heavy-duty flared flat-steel grating rather than standard wire mesh. Confirm exact beam profile (box beam versus step beam), frame depth, and required load rating per individual mesh panel—all checked against SEMA standards during our free site survey.

title: Racking Accessories

sections.heading: What Is Racking Accessories?
sections.body: Racking Accessories are purpose-built structural protection guards, load containment screens, pallet support bars, and compliance fittings designed to safeguard warehouse pallet racking from forklift collisions and prevent goods from falling off high storage beams. Even the most carefully driven warehouse experiences tight forklift turns at aisle ends, slight tine misalignments at height, and fragile shrink-wrapped pallets overhanging rear walkways. Without dedicated protection, a single minor forklift knock can twist a load-bearing upright frame into a SEMA Red Risk requiring immediate off-loading. Racking Accessories solve this by absorbing mechanical impacts before they reach structural steelwork and securing unstable loads safely inside every bay.

sections.heading: How Racking Accessories Works
sections.body: Each category of Racking Accessory addresses a specific mechanical hazard inside the warehouse. Floor-bolted steel upright protectors (column guards) and heavy tubular rack-end crash barriers sit immediately in front of vulnerable upright posts and aisle corners, transferring forklift kinetic energy straight into heavy M12/M16 floor anchors rather than the cold-rolled rack leg. Drop-in steel pallet support bars and fork spacers sit across front and rear beams to support poorly boarded pallets or allow flat sheet goods to be lifted without pallets. Rear anti-collapse steel mesh screens bracket onto the back of single-entry runs to stop toppled cartons falling into adjacent pedestrian walkways.

sections.heading: Where Racking Accessories Is Used
sections.body: Racking Accessories are mandatory safety upgrades across every busy UK warehousing environment. Fast-moving 3PL and haulage distribution centres fit heavy-duty tubular end-of-aisle barriers and individual column guards to protect high-traffic cross-aisles from counterbalance and reach truck impacts. E-commerce and retail fulfilment warehouses install rear anti-collapse wire mesh screens wherever packing benches or pedestrian walkways run behind high-bay pallet racking. Manufacturing and engineering stores use drop-in H-section pallet support bars and fork entry bars to store heavy un-palletised machinery packs and metal sheet bundles. Cold storage facilities use high-visibility polymer and steel rack guards to prevent skid impacts on icy floors, while chemical depots fit drum chocks and load notices.

sections.heading: Key Considerations
sections.body: When specifying Racking Accessories, always prioritise SEMA guidelines, which mandate upright protection on all corner posts adjacent to gangways and busy turning intersections. Remember that floor-fixed independent column protectors transfer impact energy into the slab rather than clipping onto the upright itself, though you must allow 50mm to 75mm clearance so the guard does not narrow your critical forklift aisle width. Our engineers inspect every vulnerability during a free site survey.
